judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit under the same BASIC 1 Content Standard B1.2.1.2 'Manipulate the sounds of the letters of English' (Strand 2: Reading, Sub-Strand 1: Pre-Reading Activities), so the pair is judged within one statement-type grain and at equal coordinate rank (BASIC 1, rank 0). The evidence supports a substantive same-rank developmental direction rather than mere repetition: B1.2.1.2.2 requires orally segmenting spoken syllables/words into individual sounds (LC 'Segment syllables/words into sounds'; tags oral, phonemes, segmenting), i.e. isolating discrete phonemes in a word. B1.2.1.2.3 requires saying the new word after deleting, adding or substituting an initial, middle or final sound (LCs for phoneme deletion, addition and substitution), which presupposes the learner can already isolate the target phoneme position within the word and then reassemble the remaining sounds. Proficiency in segmentation therefore supports success in phoneme manipulation, so the source is the segmentation indicator. Shared code prefix, page 39 proximity and the 'sounds' token overlap are only weak nomination signals and were not treated as sufficient on their own.
